events.title: North Dakota and South Dakota Admitted to the Union
events.description: On this day, North Dakota and South Dakota became the 39th and 40th states of the United States. President Benjamin Harrison signed the proclamations after shuffling the papers so that the order of admission could not be known, and the order was left officially undetermined.
events.significance: The admission of the Dakotas marked a major step in the settlement and political organization of the northern Great Plains and added four U.S. Senate seats, strengthening Republican influence in Congress.

events.title: Balfour Declaration Issued
events.description: British Foreign Secretary Arthur James Balfour sent a letter to Lord Rothschild expressing the British government's support for the establishment of a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine, provided the rights of existing non-Jewish communities were not prejudiced.
events.significance: The declaration became a foundational document in the history of Palestine, the Zionist movement, and the Arab-Israeli conflict, with consequences that continue to shape the Middle East.

events.title: Hughes H-4 Hercules 'Spruce Goose' Makes Its Only Flight
events.description: Howard Hughes piloted the enormous wooden H-4 Hercules flying boat for about one mile over Long Beach Harbor in California, at an altitude of roughly 70 feet, in its sole flight.
events.significance: The aircraft, with the largest wingspan of any aircraft of its era, remains a symbol of ambitious engineering and aviation history.

events.title: First Scheduled Commercial Radio Broadcast
events.description: Pittsburgh station KDKA began broadcasting the results of the Harding-Cox U.S. presidential election, widely regarded as the first scheduled commercial radio broadcast in the United States.
events.significance: KDKA's broadcast launched the era of mass radio communication, transforming news, entertainment, advertising, and political life in the 20th century.

events.title: Birth of Marie Antoinette
events.description: Marie Antoinette, the Archduchess of Austria and later Queen of France as wife of Louis XVI, was born in Vienna. She was executed by guillotine in 1793 during the French Revolution.
events.significance: Her life and execution became emblematic of the fall of the French monarchy and the radical turn of the French Revolution.
